requirements.quote:
This network
   reachability information includes information on the list of
   Autonomous Systems (ASes) that reachability information traverses.
requirements.condition: When exchanging network reachability information with other BGP systems.
requirements.required_behavior: Include the list of Autonomous Systems traversed by that reachability information.
requirements.why_checkable: The advertised reachability information can be inspected for its AS traversal information.

requirements.quote:
In the context of this document, we assume that a BGP speaker
   advertises to its peers only those routes that it uses itself (in
   this context, a BGP speaker is said to "use" a BGP route if it is the
   most preferred BGP route and is used in forwarding).  All other cases
   are outside the scope of this document.
requirements.condition: For route advertisements within the operational scope assumed by this document.
requirements.required_behavior: Advertise only routes that are the most preferred BGP routes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Advertise a BGP route that is not the most preferred BGP route within this assumed operating model.
requirements.why_checkable: The advertised route can be compared with the local BGP best-route selection.

requirements.quote:
In the context of this document, we assume that a BGP speaker
   advertises to its peers only those routes that it uses itself (in
   this context, a BGP speaker is said to "use" a BGP route if it is the
   most preferred BGP route and is used in forwarding).  All other cases
   are outside the scope of this document.
requirements.condition: For route advertisements within the operational scope assumed by this document.
requirements.required_behavior: Advertise only BGP routes used in forwarding.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Advertise a BGP route that is not used in forwarding within this assumed operating model.
requirements.why_checkable: Advertisement state can be compared with forwarding use of the selected route.

requirements.quote:
In the context of this document, the term "IP address" refers to an
   IP Version 4 address [RFC791].
requirements.condition: When interpreting IP address fields defined by this document.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret an IP address as an IPv4 address.
requirements.why_checkable: The address representation and parser family can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
Routing information exchanged via BGP supports only the destination-
   based forwarding paradigm, which assumes that a router forwards a
   packet based solely on the destination address carried in the IP
   header of the packet.
requirements.condition: For the forwarding paradigm represented by routing information exchanged via BGP.
requirements.required_behavior: Support destination-based forwarding, where the forwarding choice is based solely on the destination address in the IP header.
requirements.why_checkable: The route key and represented forwarding model can be checked for destination-address selection.

requirements.quote:
BGP-4 provides a new set of mechanisms for supporting Classless
   Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) [RFC1518, RFC1519].  These mechanisms
   include support for advertising a set of destinations as an IP prefix
   and eliminating the concept of a network "class" within BGP.
requirements.condition: When representing destinations in BGP-4 advertisements.
requirements.required_behavior: Support advertising a set of destinations as an IP prefix.
requirements.why_checkable: Advertisement encoding can be checked for IP prefix representation.

requirements.quote:
BGP-4 provides a new set of mechanisms for supporting Classless
   Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) [RFC1518, RFC1519].  These mechanisms
   include support for advertising a set of destinations as an IP prefix
   and eliminating the concept of a network "class" within BGP.
requirements.condition: When representing destinations in BGP-4.
requirements.required_behavior: Use classless routing representations.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Depend on a network class to represent BGP destination prefixes.
requirements.why_checkable: Prefix handling can be inspected for class-based assumptions.

requirements.quote:
BGP-4
   also introduces mechanisms that allow aggregation of routes,
   including aggregation of AS paths.
requirements.condition: For BGP-4 route aggregation capability.
requirements.required_behavior: Provide mechanisms allowing aggregation of routes.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation can be checked for support for forming aggregate routes.

requirements.quote:
BGP-4
   also introduces mechanisms that allow aggregation of routes,
   including aggregation of AS paths.
requirements.condition: For BGP-4 route aggregation capability.
requirements.required_behavior: Provide mechanisms allowing aggregation of AS paths.
requirements.why_checkable: AS path aggregation support has concrete input and output path representations.

requirements.quote: BGP uses TCP [RFC793] as its transport protocol.
requirements.condition: For BGP transport.
requirements.required_behavior: Use TCP as the transport protocol.
requirements.why_checkable: The transport socket protocol can be inspected.

requirements.quote: BGP listens on TCP port 179.
requirements.condition: When listening for BGP connections.
requirements.required_behavior: Listen on TCP port 179.
requirements.why_checkable: The bound listening port and transport can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
The
   error notification mechanism used in BGP assumes that TCP supports a
   "graceful" close (i.e., that all outstanding data will be delivered
   before the connection is closed).
requirements.condition: For the TCP transport assumed by the BGP error notification mechanism.
requirements.required_behavior: Support graceful close, delivering all outstanding data before closing the connection.
requirements.why_checkable: Transport shutdown sequencing can be checked for delivery of outstanding notification data.

requirements.quote:
A TCP connection is formed between two systems.  They exchange
   messages to open and confirm the connection parameters.
requirements.condition: After forming a TCP connection between the two BGP systems.
requirements.required_behavior: Exchange messages to open and confirm the connection parameters.
requirements.why_checkable: The connection establishment exchange can be observed after TCP establishment.

requirements.quote:
The initial data flow is the portion of the BGP routing table that is
   allowed by the export policy, called the Adj-Ribs-Out (see 3.2).
requirements.condition: For the initial BGP data flow.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the portion of the BGP routing table allowed by export policy, the Adj-Ribs-Out.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Include routes disallowed by export policy in the initial data flow.
requirements.why_checkable: The initial advertised routes can be compared with the export-policy-filtered table.

requirements.quote: Incremental updates are sent as the routing tables change.
requirements.condition: As routing tables change.
requirements.required_behavior: Send incremental updates.
requirements.why_checkable: Route-table changes can be correlated with generated update messages.

requirements.quote:
BGP does
   not require a periodic refresh of the routing table.
requirements.condition: For ongoing BGP routing-table exchange.
requirements.required_behavior: Operate without requiring periodic refresh of the routing table.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Require a periodic routing-table refresh as a prerequisite for continued BGP operation.
requirements.why_checkable: A stable session can be checked for dependency on periodic whole-table refresh.

requirements.quote:
To allow local
   policy changes to have the correct effect without resetting any BGP
   connections, a BGP speaker SHOULD either (a) retain the current
   version of the routes advertised to it by all of its peers for the
   duration of the connection, or (b) make use of the Route Refresh
   extension [RFC2918].
requirements.condition: To allow local policy changes to have the correct effect without resetting BGP connections.
requirements.required_behavior: A BGP speaker SHOULD either retain the current version of routes advertised by all peers for the duration of each connection, or use the Route Refresh extension.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation can be checked for either current per-peer route retention or Route Refresh support and use.

requirements.quote:
KEEPALIVE messages may be sent periodically to ensure that the
   connection is live.
requirements.condition: To ensure that the connection is live.
requirements.required_behavior: KEEPALIVE messages may be sent periodically.
requirements.why_checkable: The optional periodic KEEPALIVE transmission path and timer are observable.

requirements.quote:
If a connection encounters an error
   condition, a NOTIFICATION message is sent and the connection is
   closed.
requirements.condition: If a connection encounters an error condition.
requirements.required_behavior: Send a NOTIFICATION message.
requirements.error_behavior: Send a NOTIFICATION message for the connection error.
requirements.why_checkable: The error-handling branch can be checked for notification emission.

requirements.quote:
If a connection encounters an error
   condition, a NOTIFICATION message is sent and the connection is
   closed.
requirements.condition: If a connection encounters an error condition.
requirements.required_behavior: Close the connection.
requirements.error_behavior: Close the connection after sending the NOTIFICATION message.
requirements.why_checkable: The error-handling path can be checked for transport closure after notification.

requirements.quote:
A peer in a different AS is referred to as an external peer, while a
   peer in the same AS is referred to as an internal peer.
requirements.condition: When the peer is in a different AS.
requirements.required_behavior: Classify the peer as external.
requirements.why_checkable: Peer type can be compared with local and peer AS identifiers.

requirements.quote:
A peer in a different AS is referred to as an external peer, while a
   peer in the same AS is referred to as an internal peer.
requirements.condition: When the peer is in the same AS.
requirements.required_behavior: Classify the peer as internal.
requirements.why_checkable: Peer type can be compared with local and peer AS identifiers.

requirements.quote:
If a particular AS has multiple BGP speakers and is providing transit
   service for other ASes, then care must be taken to ensure a
   consistent view of routing within the AS.  A consistent view of the
   interior routes of the AS is provided by the IGP used within the AS.
   For the purpose of this document, it is assumed that a consistent
   view of the routes exterior to the AS is provided by having all BGP
   speakers within the AS maintain IBGP with each other.
requirements.condition: Within the operational model assumed by this document, an AS has multiple BGP speakers and provides transit service for other ASes.
requirements.required_behavior: Have all BGP speakers within the AS maintain IBGP with each other to provide the assumed consistent view of exterior routes.
requirements.why_checkable: The configured and maintained internal peering graph can be checked for pairwise IBGP connectivity under the stated operating-model assumption.
